[TOC]



At present, there are three kinds of code terms at the beginning of standard documents formulated in China:

**GB**

Full name: National Standard (Guo Biao)

Definition: Approved and issued by the competent authority for standardization administration of the People's Republic of China; a standard of great significance to the national economic and technological development that is unified nationwide.

Nature: Mandatory standard. Such standards have legal significance and must be implemented. Products that do not conform to mandatory standards are prohibited from production, sale and import.

Application scope: Widely used in production, scientific research and other fields; it is directly related to public interests, aiming to protect public safety, promote economic development and improve product quality.

**GB/T**

Full name: Recommended National Standard (T stands for recommended)

Definition: A type of standard voluntarily adopted through economic means or market regulation in production, exchange and use, also called a voluntary standard.

Nature: Not legally enforceable. However, once a recommended national standard is accepted and adopted, or included in an economic contract, it becomes legally binding.

Application scope: Covers various industries and fields such as machinery, electronics, construction, food and medicine. It aims to promote the development of standardization work and improve the quality of products and services.

**JT/T**

Full name: Recommended Standard for the Transportation Industry (T stands for recommended)

Definition: A recommended standard issued by the Ministry of Transport or relevant institutions in the transportation industry.

Nature: Similar to GB/T, it is not legally enforceable, but once accepted and adopted by the industry or enterprises, it is somewhat binding.

Application scope: Specifically applied to the transportation industry, such as road transport, water transport and air transport, aiming to regulate technical activities in the industry and improve the quality and efficiency of transportation services.

**GB/Z**

Full name: National Standardization Guiding Technical Document (Z stands for guiding)

Definition: A guiding technical document added outside the national standard system to meet the needs of rapid development and rapid change of standards in certain fields, as a supplement to national standards.

Nature: It has neither legal force nor legal binding force. It only provides technical guidance for relevant parties and plays a role in guiding and regulating a certain activity.

Application scope: Mainly used to guide technical activities in the fields of production, exchange and use, and to provide reference for relevant personnel in scientific research, design, production, use and management.

**GB is a mandatory national standard** and must be implemented.

**GB/T and JT/T are recommended national standard documents**, voluntarily adopted through economic means or market regulation, but once accepted and adopted or included in an economic contract, they become legally binding.

**GB/Z is a national standardization guiding technical document**, for reference by users only, and is neither mandatory nor legally binding.

**Examples**

Mandatory standard document: **GB 14887-2011** (Road traffic signal lamps)

Recommended national standard document: **GB/T 28181-2022** (Technical requirements for information transmission, switch and control in video surveillance networking system for public security)

**JTT808-2019** (Industry standard of the Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China)

National standardization guiding technical document: **GB/Z 17977-2000** (Information technology - Telecommunications and information exchange between systems - OSI Routing Framework)
